content.text:
`npm test` ran 10 tests: 7 pass and 3 fail. All three failures come from the latest commit (`fa2a6cb "broken"`), which changed one query filter in each of three service files. I didn't change anything.

| Failing test | Where | Why it fails |
|---|---|---|
| `findByEmail ignores soft-deleted users` | `tests/auth-service.test.js:5` | `src/services/auth-service.js:5` no longer has the `&& u.deleted_at === null` check. Looking up `alan@example.com`, a soft-deleted user, now returns that user when the test expects `null`. |
| `totalPaidCents counts only paid orders` | `tests/order-service.test.js:14` | `src/services/order-service.js:9` now filters on `o.status === 'quote'` instead of `'paid'`. It returns **1350** when the test expects **14600**. |
| `uncapturedTotalCents sums uncaptured payments` | `tests/payment-service.test.js:14` | `src/services/payment-service.js:10` now filters on `p.captured === true` instead of `false`, so it adds up the captured payments. It returns **4200** when the test expects **9900**. |

The error output for the order and payment failures is confusing to read, and here's why. The test's assertion inside the callback fails first (e.g. `1350 !== 14600`). The `try/catch` in `query()` (`src/db.js:32-36`) catches that error and calls the same callback a second time, now with the error as `err`. The test's first check, `assert.equal(err, null)`, then fails too. So the report says "expected `null`, got AssertionError," with the real value mismatch nested inside it.

The 7 passing tests are the repository tests, the user-service tests, `isActive`, `listOrdersForUser` and `findPaymentsForOrder`. The repository tests (`UserRepository.findActive`, `OrderRepository.findPaid`) pass because they test the repository classes, not the broken service functions.
